R3104/3–4 bywm ts¹ʿm “on the ninth day (lit. Day Nine)” of the month; J735/5 “on the ninth (year of his eponymate)”; J577/15 sbʿ w-ts¹ʿy “ninety-seven wells”. Read from the OCR text; check the page image.

The ninth hour of the day was “the hour of prayer” at the temple (Act 3:1), and Cornelius was praying at it when he was told that his prayers and his alms had “come up for a memorial before God” (Act 3:1; 10:3–4, 30–31). Scripture sets prayer at the time of the evening offering by the verses that set prayer at that offering (1Ki 18:36; Ezr 9:5; Dan 9:21; Psa 141:2). From the sixth hour there was darkness over the land “until the ninth hour”, and “about the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice”, and gave up his spirit (Mat 27:45–46, 50; Mar 15:33–37; Luk 23:44–46). So Christ died at the hour when Israel prayed and the evening offering was made: the offering that those daily offerings looked to (Heb 10:10–12).

Root key תשע: the database files the three words under root key תקפ (BDB w.bq.bn תֵּשַׁע, w.bq.bo תְּשִׁיעִי, w.bq.bp תִּשְׁעִים), lumped with the other words at the end of BDB’s ת section by page order; the entry takes the words’ own consonants, as bad.json does for linen. BDB’s תֵּשַׁע key also holds the date uses (Lev 23:32, 2Ki 18:10, 25:3, Jer 39:2, 52:6, 2Ki 15:13, 15:17), given here as a sense of the cardinal with kin to the ordinal. No Biblical Aramaic word for nine. Sounds: Arabic, Ugaritic and Sabaean show š and ʿ; Aramaic ש rules out ṯ; no cognate shows ṯ or ġ, so no split. Segert p. 53 and p. 204 and Biella p. 535 were read from the OCR text only (Segert’s numeral table is badly garbled); Krahmalkov p. 499 from the text extraction; check the page images. Ge’ez is from Wiktionary only; check Dillmann and Leslau. SEDRA lexeme 3455 (TWE;N, root 2002 TWE) glosses ninety also “lot; portion”, which no New Testament verse shows; not recorded. SEDRA lexeme 3454 TWE “nine”. Lane’s تُسْع “a ninth part” and the verb “take the ninth part” are not named on any word: scripture’s feminine תְּשִׁיעִית is only the ordinal. The doctrine “the-ninth-hour” ties the hour of prayer (Act 3:1) to the time of the evening offering by the verses that set prayer at that offering; scripture does not itself name the ninth hour as the hour of the offering. Not written: any doctrine from nine as a number in itself, or a reading of Dan 12:11’s 1290 days; scripture draws neither from this word.

analysis.evidence: In חָמֵשׁ וְתִשְׁעִים שָׁנָה, ‘five and ninety years’, the marked numeral supplies the ninety in ninety-five. The following וַחֲמֵשׁ מֵאֹת שָׁנָה adds five hundred years, giving 595 years of Lamech’s life after Noah’s birth.
analysis.morphology: Prefixed conjunction וְ ‘and’ + cardinal numeral, common gender, plural absolute.

analysis.evidence: In חָמֵשׁ וְתִשְׁעִים שָׁנָה, the marked noun supplies the unit for ‘ninety-five.’ Together with the following five hundred years, it measures how long Lamech lived after he fathered Noah.
